title: Typed Forms and User Input knowledge check

questions.prompt: What should a typed frontend still validate?
options: Nothing: JSX and TypeScript guarantee every browser value is valid.
The frontend can decide server authorization by itself.
Only CSS class names need types.
User input and server responses at runtime, while keeping loading, success and failure states explicit.
questions.answer_key: User input and server responses at runtime, while keeping loading, success and failure states explicit.
questions.explanation: Typed UI models improve development feedback but do not replace runtime validation or server-side checks.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Typed Forms and User Input”?
options: A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with input value types and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with input value types and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Input value types”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Typed Forms and User Input”?
options: Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check form state, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume runtime validation of submitted values is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
questions.answer_key: Check form state, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Form state”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
